name: Bio-based chemicals (bio-ethylene, bio-PE, PLA)
principle: Sugarcane ethanol is dehydrated to ethylene and polymerised to polyethylene identical to fossil PE (Braskem Green PE, Triunfo, 200,000 t/yr since 2010); lactic acid from sugars is polymerised to PLA. IEA rates ethylene production by fermentation at TRL 9.

source.note: Wikipedia, Renewable polyethylene, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

performance.metric: CO2 sequestered per tonne Green PE
performance.basis: general figure for Green PE, not Braskem-specific

source.note: Wikipedia, Renewable polyethylene, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)
Wikipedia, Renewable polyethylene, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

reference_plants.name: NatureWorks Ingeo PLA plant, Blair, Nebraska
reference_plants.capacity: nameplate 140,000 t/yr (300 million lb), world's first and largest PLA plant (doubled to full design capacity by 2009)

source.note: C&EN, 13 Jul 2009 (doubling to 140,000 t/yr design capacity); read 2026-10-28

reference_plants.name: NatureWorks Ingeo PLA plant, Rayong, Thailand
reference_plants.capacity: 75,000 t/yr; construction milestone Feb 2023, production planned from 2025

source.note: IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, latest assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'Ethylene production using fermentation' 9 (2025)

advantages: Drop-in with fossil PE and recyclable in existing streams

sources.note: Wikipedia, Renewable polyethylene, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)
C&EN, NatureWorks ups PLA capacity, 13 Jul 2009
